correctness.rationale: For n≥5, cubic triangle-free M2n has exactly six connected induced 4-vertex set families S,R,E−,E+,M,Q with 2n copies of each of the first five and n distinct squares Q (11n total). A dual face of size 5 would induce a 2-vertex-connected triangle-free 5-vertex graph: absence of 5-cycles by spoke/rim displacement forces a square, and the fifth vertex would need two opposite square neighbors, producing K2,3 and three common neighbors, impossible in M2n. Thus the Alexander dual is a full 2-skeleton plus exactly 11n tetrahedra. The explicit six families of free triangular faces are checked in the order S,R,E−,E+,M,Q, collapsing each tetrahedron without creating an omitted coface. The dual remains simply connected after deleting free tetrahedron/triangle pairs, with reduced H2 free rank binom(2n−1,3)−11n by Euler characteristic; Hurewicz and Whitehead yield a 2-sphere wedge. Integral Alexander duality supplies primal homology only in degree 2n−5; absence of any 5-vertex dual face implies the primal contains a complete (2n−6)-skeleton, and successive connectivity/Hurewicz then yield exactly the asserted wedge of (2n−5)-spheres. Independently reconstructed the frozen Git tree from all seven blob SHAs. A separately written checker exhaustively regenerated every connected four-set and verified all written free triangles for each n=5..14; checked every possible five-set for n=5..10; first ranks 29,99,209. These finite checks corroborate but do not replace the unbounded proof.
residual_risks: The uniform proof depends essentially on n≥5: spoke displacement, the absence of 5-cycles, and uniqueness of listed four-vertex families; it is not asserted for n=4 or smaller.
Finite stress tests n5..14 are not exhaustive for all n, and no Lean proof or expert attestation is claimed.
No equivariant homotopy type, shellability result, or total-cut statement follows automatically.

value.rationale: The ordinary four-cut complex of the natural infinite Möbius ladder graph family is a mathematically motivated exact integral topological invariant, explicitly proposed among interesting cut-complex directions by Agarwal–Basak Problem 26. The theorem identifies every n≥5 homotopy type, its sphere degree 2n−5 and a nontrivial cubic polynomial multiplicity binom(2n−1,3)−11n, not simply an Euler number or sampled finite table. Its constructive uniform six-family free-triangle collapse also supplies an independently usable structural reduction beyond applying a textbook Euler identity. Earlier work treats the same graph under a different total-cut condition or rectangular/circular ladders under other ordinary parameters, so the exact fact would be useful for later graph-cut topology and comparative homotopy work.
residual_risks: No theorem for arbitrary cubic graphs, other cut parameters, or equivariant character is established or necessary for the value of this exact family classification.
Potential independently published equivalent classification would change the originality assessment.
